concept.name: Tokenomics
concept.definition: Tokenomics is the economic design of a crypto token: its supply schedule (issuance, burns, caps), distribution (allocations, vesting, airdrops), utility (fees, governance, staking) and the incentive structures that determine how value and behavior accrue around it.
concept.intuition: It is the monetary policy plus cap table plus business model of a token — the rules that decide who gets tokens, when, and why anyone should hold them.
concept.mechanics: Core levers include fixed vs inflationary supply and emission schedules, allocation splits across community/team/investors with vesting, burn or buyback mechanisms, and utility sinks (fee capture, staking, governance). These parameters are set in the whitepaper or governance and drive circulating supply dynamics, dilution and sell-pressure over time.
concept.failure_modes: Low-float/high-FDV designs with heavy insider allocations create structural overhang: unlocks and emissions overwhelm demand; unsustainable incentive emissions fund short-term growth at the cost of long-term dilution and death spirals.
concept.misconceptions: A capped supply does not guarantee scarcity value — emission timing and insider concentration matter more than the headline cap. Price appreciation is not a tokenomics success metric; design quality shows in distribution fairness and sustainable value accrual.
concept.example: Uniswap's UNI: 1B minted at genesis, 60% to the community, 21.3% to team and 18% to investors on 4-year vesting, 15% retroactively airdropped to users, and a 2% perpetual inflation after year 4 — a complete tokenomic specification in one announcement.

citations.source: Keyrock research - From Locked to Liquidity: What 16,000+ Token Unlocks Teach Us
